definition_of_done_items.criterion: Non-transactional compose mail (marked marketing) checks blocksMarketing per recipient within the tenant and skips it with an audit entry
Mail not marked as marketing or service is not sent to an objector: the sender must say it is a service email first (codex-review finding, ifc315-r3)
Workflow and automation: no email send step exists (workflow custom actions POST to a tenant webhook only)
Auto-response drafts refuse any restricted person, which includes a marketing objection (test added)
Transactional mail (booking confirmations, DSAR notices) still sends
Completing a marketing objection no longer requires a manual stop; the stop method is optional
The completion audit row records marketingStopped from the request (marketing objection), and whether an external stop method was given
The person is told only what the CRM enforces: its CRM will no longer send them marketing email

notes: No migration: blocksMarketing already exists on processing_restrictions. The send guard lives in dispatchUserMail, the only path that sends to a lead or contact address the user chooses. Refused sends are audited as email_message / EmailMarketingObjectionApplied with counts only; the addresses stay on the email record metadata, as suppressed addresses already do. Re-gate fix (codex-review r3): an email with no purpose to anyone who objected is refused (PURPOSE_REQUIRED) and compose offers "Send as a service email" or "Send as marketing", so the objection no longer depends on the sender ticking a box.
